# The three INPUTS of StrongRowView.gatedRate and the OUTPUT it produced, one
# line per recorded second, for three rows written by this app. Read by
# scripts/lock_snap_replay.py; every figure #193 and its pull request quote is
# derived from this file.
#
# FORMAT
#   ROW <key> <label>                       starts a row
#   REC <rate_raw> <lock_rate> <rate_base> <row_stroke_rate>
#                                           one recorded second, in timestamp
#                                           order, all four in spm
#   Lines beginning with # and blank lines are ignored.
#
# WHY FOUR COLUMNS ON ONE LINE, when scripts/fixtures/cue_work_laps.txt holds
# one series and its companion holds the other. gatedRate's ARGUMENT LIST is
# the tuple (median rate, lock period, established rate): the three are read in
# the same call, and a replay that paired a median with a lock from a different
# second would be replaying a machine that never ran. Here alignment is
# intrinsic to the line rather than checked across files. `row_stroke_rate` is
# the fourth column because it is what the call RETURNED -- it is the target
# the transcription is proved against, not a fifth input.
#
# The scoring selectors that gatedRate never sees -- step_type and
# enhanced_speed -- are NOT here. They are in the companion,
# scripts/fixtures/lock_snap_context.txt, for the reason lock_guard_speed.txt
# states for itself: a series the decision never reads must not be able to move
# a figure the decision produces.
#
# PROVENANCE, so this is reproducible from the originals with any FIT decoder:
#   source files   i183553852.fit, i178249719.fit, i174014735.fit
#   values         the developer fields of record messages (FIT global message
#                  20), in timestamp order, no lap filtering of any kind:
#                    rate_raw         developer field id 23
#                    lock_rate        developer field id 20
#                    rate_base        developer field id 24
#                    row_stroke_rate  developer field id 0
#   selection      a record is written here only if it carries ALL FOUR. That
#                  drops 1 record of i178249719's 3003 and none of the other
#                  two rows'.
#   lock period    lock_rate is the RATE. gatedRate takes a PERIOD, so the
#                  replay passes 60/lock_rate and 0.0 for no lock -- the same
#                  inverse StrongRowView.lockRateOf applies on the way out.
#   precision      float32 in the file, written here to 6 decimal places with
#                  trailing zeros stripped. Measured, not assumed: at 6 dp no
#                  record's branch decision or output moves under the shipped
#                  rule or under the guard at any tolerance in 0.07-0.15; at
#                  5 dp and at 4 dp, two records of i183553852 flip branch.
#
# ABSENCE. No record written here is MISSING any of the four columns -- that is
# what the selection rule above guarantees -- so this file needs no absence
# marker, which is stated rather than left to be noticed. A 0 is never absence
# here either; each column has its own in-band meaning for it, and they are not
# the same meaning:
#   rate_raw         0 is "the stroke ring has timed out or nothing has been
#                    measured". It is not a 0 spm cadence.
#   lock_rate        0 is LOCK_RATE_NONE, the app's NO-LOCK sentinel. A real
#                    lock is a rate in [MIN_RATE, MAX_RATE] = [6, 40], so 0 is
#                    out of band by construction (updateAutocorr searches only
#                    lags in [60/MAX_RATE, 60/MIN_RATE]).
#   rate_base        0 is RATE_BASE_NONE, "no established rate yet".
#   row_stroke_rate  0 is the app's NO-DATA sentinel: outputRate() returns 0.0
#                    when nothing has been measured and drawRate renders it
#                    "--.-". The same convention cue_work_laps.txt states.
#
# CROSS-CHECKS a reader can run against the originals, all pinned by
# scripts/test_lock_snap_replay.py:
#   records written           i183553852 3385, i178249719 3002, i174014735 2276
#   the shipped gatedRate replayed from columns 1-3 reproduces column 4 on
#                             3382/3385, 2997/3002 and 2274/2276 records
#   snaps fired (the shipped rule substituting the lock)
#                             643, 356 and 175
#   i183553852 record 2489    rate_raw 18.518518, lock_rate 6.383, output 6.383
#   i183553852 record 2503    rate_raw 10.416667, lock_rate 33.333, output
#                             33.333
#
# THE TEN RECORDS THAT DO NOT REPRODUCE ARE AN UNEXPLAINED RESIDUAL (#194),
# recorded here rather than attributed. Three of them -- i183553852 1490 and
# 3340, i178249719 2941 -- are reproduced exactly by the shipped gatedRate
# evaluated with the NEXT record's lock_rate, i.e. the recorded output is one
# lock update ahead of the recorded lock. The obvious mechanism is RULED OUT at
# source: onTick writes row_stroke_rate at source/StrongRowView.mc:1982 and the
# diagnostics at :2163-2191, both inside the one `if (mStarted && !mPaused)`
# block that opens at :1981 and closes at :2380 (verified at d2cd8a6), and
# nothing between them touches mRate or mAcPeriod. Nothing in this repository
# decodes a file this app wrote, so the cause is not answerable from here.
# scripts/lock_snap_replay.py `reproduce` prints the residual list rather than
# rounding it away, and every figure taken from this fixture is computed from
# the REPLAYED series so the residual cannot contaminate a before/after pair.
ROW i183553852 8x3' strength-endurance, the row #193 was reported from
